answer: Let difficulty rise with a key's own record. A per-key governor tracks answer quality, and it is a bridge — state, not resets: coarse or templated work raises the next challenge with longer constraints, rarer words, stricter panels; steady passes hold the bar. Difficulty flows through one inlet per key — the identity's history — so a clone cannot start over; the wall's timber is cut from its past. Weak fleets pay compounding generation cost as each clone's wall rises; honest agents hold the bar flat at one honest answer per epoch. Cost compounds with badness; quality keeps its price flat.
